title: Retrieval + Eval: scratches and ideas (Sep 2026)
content:
Quick log / scratchpad — trying to capture small experiments, heuristics, and open questions from the retrieval + eval workshop and my reading. Mostly rough; TODOs at the bottom.

High level framing (one-liner): how do we build a practical retrieval stack and evaluation loop that (1) surfaces high-signal context for low-latency LLM inference, (2) gives reliable evals for real-world QA/chat tasks, and (3) fits Redwood's production constraints (latency SLOs, cost, consistent API)?

Notes from reading (snippets, not full summaries):
- "Sparse Mixture-of-Experts for Retrieval" (arXiv 2305.xxxx) — interesting idea: route query expansion to specialized sub-indexes. Practicality note: sharding index by domain-sensitive encoders gives good precision at small latency cost if we pre-route by a fast lightweight classifier. But classifier adds complexity/failure modes.
- Dense retrievers + lexical hybrid (BM25 + dense) seems still the pragmatic sweet spot. Long tail queries (rare entity combos) often rescued by lexical signals.
- Reranker architectures: cross-encoder reranking (full attention over query+passage) improves top-1 precision significantly but kills latency. Two-stage pipeline with small lexical/dense candidate generator + tiny transformer reranker (6-12 layers, distilled) is a good middle ground.

Small experiment sketches I want to run (notes to self):
1) Candidate window size vs latency under Redwood Dedicated profile
   - baseline: dense-only retriever (1536-d) returning top-50, cross-encoder rerank top-10. measure p@1, latency tail (95th)
   - variant A: BM25 + dense union top-100 -> dedup -> rerank top-10 (expect p@1 boost for entity-Qs)
   - variant B: classifier pre-route to domain-specific dense index (3 domains) -> reduce candidate pool to top-30 -> rerank
   - logging: tag each request with candidate-source breakdown (bm25/dense/domain) for later analysis

2) Reranker quantization tradeoffs (important for Dedicated/Private)
   - run 8-bit and 4-bit quant variants of a distilled reranker; measure delta in rank quality (MRR) vs latency and memory
   - watch for calibration drift — reranker score magnitudes change after quantization, need re-scaling before thresholding/ensemble

Evaluation / metric thoughts (this is messy in practice):
- For product QA tasks, raw IR metrics (MRR, nDCG) are necessary but not sufficient. Need downstream LM answer quality: exact-match on short factoids, human-rated groundedness for open answers.
- Lightweight automatic proxy: generate answer with target model + passage attribution score (overlap features + reranker logits) -> heuristics estimate hallucination risk. This is brittle but cheap for continuous monitoring.
- Build small eval harness that runs typical prompts across candidate pipelines and computes: token cost, p@1, F1 against gold spans, and LM hallucination proxy. Do nightly runs on 50 prompt families.

Observations from Redwood infra constraints:
- Prefix/KV cache interactions: if retriever picks different passages across near-identical queries, cache hit rate collapses. We should encourage candidate stability (e.g., anchored passage selection) when latency SLOs rely on cached KV.
- Batching: reranker can be batched efficiently, but cross-encoder worst-case token lengths are tricky. Keep reranker input size bounded (truncate intelligently) and prefer passage-level scoring to long concatenated contexts.

Open questions / tension points:
- How much to invest in pre-retrieval routing (domain classifier) vs investing in a better unified retriever? Pre-routing reduces candidate size but makes failure modes more brittle (misroute).
- Where to place reranking relative to caching? If reranker is expensive, we might cache its top-1 result per query fingerprint, but queries drift (paraphrases) so fingerprinting heuristics matter.
- Eval labeling budget: do we use crowd labels for a rolling validation set or rely on automatic proxies? Crowdsourced labeling gives higher fidelity but is expensive for many prompt families.

Concrete heuristics I like (for experiments):
- Use a cheap lexical filter (BM25 top-200) as a safety net for long-tail queries, then apply dense retriever over the reduced candidate pool. This keeps cost reasonable and improves recall.
- Distill a mobile-friendly reranker for 6-layer TPU/GPU friendly inference; target <20ms per passage at batch size=8 on Dedicated profile.
- Deterministic candidate tie-break: sort by (score, doc_id) to avoid flipping between equally-scored passages and stabilize KV cache hit rates.

Fragments from workshop discussion (paraphrase):
- "We should treat retrieval itself as a model with versions and rollouts" — agrees with product: pin retriever version with model version.
- "Use eval sets that mirror production prompt distribution" — easier said than done; need sampling hooks in API.
- "Rerank calibration matters as much as rank order" — downstream ensembles and attribution heuristics rely on calibrated logits.

Notes to re-check / reading backlog: (short list)
- Re-read dense + quantization paper: arXiv:2004.14919 (for 8-bit trick details)
- Look into "index partitioning by semantic cluster" approach from recent workshop notes (slack thread id above)
- Check PR #48 in rag-experiments for the candidate-stability logging code (might need minor changes before can run nightly)

Actionable TODOs (priority order):
- [ ] Add candidate-source breakdown fields to request logs (who provided the top-1). Link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rag-experiments/pull/48 (follow-up: test in staging).
- [ ] Prototype BM25+Dense union pipeline on sample dataset (500 queries) and compute p@1 delta vs dense-only (target: >3% absolute p@1 improvement on product queries).
- [ ] Run quantized reranker experiment (8-bit/4-bit) and capture calibration shift; add rescaling if necessary.
- [ ] Build nightly eval harness (50 prompt families) and wire to console metric dashboard (product asks for token-cost + p@1 + hallucination-proxy).

Random small pro-tips for later recording:
- When deduping candidates, use normalized doc fingerprint + char-level n-gram overlap threshold (0.85) rather than exact URL dedupe; catches simple mirrors/formatting diffs.
- In pipelines where we need stable KV cache, add a soft-stable-selection step: if two candidates have score difference < epsilon, prefer previously served candidate if it exists within top-K. Implement via small LRU map keyed by query-hash.

Final quick reflection: the core difficulty isn't the retrieval model alone, it's the pipeline stability and monitoring — keeping candidate choices stable enough for caching and being able to detect regressions quickly. Most return-on-effort right now is in instrumentation + small heuristics (lexical hybrid + deterministic tie-break) rather than large model training.

If anything sparks, ping me (Ishaan) or drop notes in the slack thread. Will iterate this into a more formal playbook once the BM25+Dense runs finish.

End of scratchpad.
